newsitem.title: FRANCE: Indian freighter searches for missing Canadian.
newsitem.headline: Indian freighter searches for missing Canadian.

text.p: An Indian freighter began searching on Tuesday for lone Canadian yachtsman Gerry Roufs, who has been missing for a week in one of the most remote areas of the Pacific Ocean, French rescue service Cross Etel said.
It said the captain of the Aditya Gaurav had agreed to search the area for 24 to 36 hours on a voyage from Australia to Argentina.

Canadian authorities, meanwhile, were analysing satellite data to help locate Roufs, a competitor in the Vendee Globe round-the-world sailing race who is missing somewhere between New Zealand, South America and Antarctica.

Roufs is in a region much less accessible by rescuers than the area from which the Australian navy rescued two other race competitors, Frenchman Thierry Dubois and Briton Tony Bullimore, whose boats had capsized southwest of Australia.

He was last in contact a week ago about 2,175 miles (3,500 km) west of the southern tip of Chile, out of range of search and rescue aircraft. A cargo ship and another race competitor abandoned their search efforts last Sunday.
Ed Langham, a spokesman for the Canadian satellite programme Radarsat has said it was too early to tell whether the images being studied had captured images of Roufs' boat.

The race's French organisers said a satellite picture taken on Sunday had yielded specks suggesting about 20 possible locations. A second picture taken on Monday was being superimposed over the first one to try clarify if one of the spots could be a boat. A third satellite sweep was being prepared for Wednesday.
Langham has said the satellite could capture images through cloud or darkness, adding that, under ideal conditions, such as calm seas and low winds, it could easily pick up a boat image.
But heavy waves whipped by winds of up to 50 miles (80 km) an hour were making the South Pacific satellite images much more difficult to decipher.
